newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans seven-year trade curb phase-out - paper.
newsitem.headline: India plans seven-year trade curb phase-out - paper.

text.p: India plans to present the World Trade Organisation (WTO) with a proposal to phase out restrictions on imports within seven years, the Economic Times on Monday quoted Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah as saying.

"India will table a seven-year phase-out period for quantitative restrictions (QRs) on imports at the World Trade Organisation and will be able to get the support of all developed countries for its timetable," the daily quoted Ramaiah as saying.
"It will be impossible for India to go below a seven-year period for the removal of QRs," Ramaiah said.
The newspaper said the proposal would be presented to the trade body in Geneva next week, after Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet approved it.

Last week, talks at the WTO on the proposed elimination of India's import restrictions were suspended until June 30 after New Delhi's major trade partners objected to its initial plan to phase out curbs over nine years.

India then told the WTO Committee on Balance of Payments Restrictions it needed a phase-out period of nine years to avoid a sharp decline in foreign exchange reserves, which could trigger a balance of payments crisis.

But delegates from the European Union, the United States, Japan, Canada and Australia said India's foreign exchange reserves no longer justified the restrictions, and called for a transitional period of two to three years, not seven.
India's foreign exchange reserves for May reached $28.13 billion, compared with $21.64 billion for the year-ago period.
